new.title: Admire the tiled interior of Behram Paşa Mosque
new.desc: Built between about 1564 and 1572 for the Ottoman governor-general Behram Paşa, this is the largest Ottoman-style mosque in Diyarbakır. One of Sinan's autobiographies attributes it to him, and its local tiles closely resemble İznik work.
new.tip: Dress modestly and avoid prayer times. It sits in a residential lane south-west of the Great Mosque, so follow signs through the old streets.
new.q: Behram Paşa Camii, Fatih Paşa, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Find the blue-tiled minaret of Safa (Parlı) Mosque
new.desc: A pre-Ottoman mosque near Urfa Gate, traditionally linked to the Akkoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan, with an inscription recording a repair in 1531-32. Its prayer hall has a large dome on four piers and its stone minaret carries blue glazed tiles.
new.tip: Combine it with the walk along the walls to Urfa Kapı. Visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Parlı Safa Camii, Azizoğlu Sokak, Melikahmet Mahallesi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Walk through Deliller Han, the 1527 caravanserai at Mardin Gate
new.desc: Deli Hüsrev Paşa, the second Ottoman governor of Diyarbakır, built this han in 1527-28; it is named after the guides (deliller) who lodged pilgrims here. Restored in the 1980s, it now runs as a hotel around its stone courtyard.
new.tip: Non-guests can usually look at the courtyard and arcades; ask at reception. It stands just inside Mardin Kapı.
new.q: Deliller Hanı, Mardin Kapı, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Visit the Ahmet Arif Literature Museum Library
new.desc: A restored courtyard house of about 120 years in Sur, run by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and dedicated to the poet Ahmet Arif (1927-1991). It holds an archive and library of Turkish literature and is one of the city's finest civil-architecture examples.
new.tip: Check opening hours locally before going; it is a quiet stop between the Tarancı and Gökalp houses.
new.q: Ahmet Arif Edebiyat Müzesi Kütüphanesi, Ziya Gökalp Sokak, Cami Kebir Mahallesi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Cross the Haburman Bridge of 1179 near Çermik
new.desc: An Artuqid stone bridge over the Sinek stream, commissioned in 1179 by Zübeyde Hatun, daughter of the Artuqid ruler Necmeddin Alpı. Road traffic was moved to a new bridge in 2010, so the old arch can be seen on foot.
new.tip: Best in spring when the stream runs high. It lies about 90 km from Diyarbakır, near Haburman village.

new.title: Hike to the Twin Waterfalls in Yabanardı, Çermik
new.desc: Two waterfalls linked by a trail of about 1 km in Yabanardı neighbourhood, with smaller cascades along the stream, a mill over 250 years old and wild goats in the surrounding rocks. It is promoted as part of the Mesopotamian golden-triangle nature route.
new.tip: Go in spring or early summer for water and shade, wear shoes with grip, and ask locals for the track in Yabanardı.
new.q: İkiz Şelale, Yabanardı Mahallesi, Çermik, Diyarbakır

new.title: Walk to Timsah (Crocodile) Canyon near Dicle
new.desc: A rock formation in Taşağıl neighbourhood, about 62 km from Diyarbakır, whose outline resembles a crocodile. It is reached after a roughly ten-minute walk through oak woodland and is popular for picnics and photography.
new.tip: Greenest after spring rains; take water and sturdy shoes, as there are no facilities.
new.q: Timsah Kanyonu, Taşağıl Mahallesi, Dicle, Diyarbakır

new.title: Climb to Kefrun Castle above Kulp
new.desc: A rock-built fortress in Konuklu neighbourhood of Kulp, said to be around 5,000 years old and notable for brick walls, the only brick fortification of its kind in the Diyarbakır region. It overlooks the Tigris basin and has cistern remains.
new.tip: Drive to the village and walk the last stretch. It is remote, about 170 km from the city, so combine with Lice or Bırkleyn.
new.q: Kefrun Kalesi, Konuklu Mahallesi, Kulp, Diyarbakır

new.title: Visit the 5th-century Mor Kiryakus Monastery in Beşiri
new.desc: A two-storey Syriac Christian monastery of about 2,500 square metres on the slopes of Mount Kıra in Ayrancı village, Beşiri, dated to the 5th century. It was restored in three phases and reopened to visitors with a ceremony.
new.tip: Confirm access with Batman's culture office as hours are not widely published. Do not confuse it with Mor Aho near Gercüş.
new.q: Mor Kiryakus Manastırı, Ayrancı Köyü, Beşiri, Batman

new.title: See Er-Rızk Mosque, moved whole to New Hasankeyf
new.desc: Built in 1409 under the Ayyubids, this mosque was lifted as a 1,700-tonne block in 2019 and carried on a special platform to the new Cultural Park to escape the Ilısu reservoir. It stands there with the relocated Zeynel Bey Tomb and other monuments.
new.tip: Visit with the Hasankeyf Museum next door; there is little shade, so go early or late.
new.q: Er-Rızk Camii, Hasankeyf Kültür Parkı, Hasankeyf, Batman

new.title: Eat grilled liver at Meşhur Ciğerci Çavuş in Batman
new.desc: Grilled liver (ızgara ciğer) is Batman's best-known dish, served with onions, sumac, greens and fresh bread. Ciğerci Çavuş in the central İkiztepe area is one of the best-rated liver shops in the city.
new.tip: Liver is a breakfast and lunch food, so go before mid-afternoon.
new.q: Ciğerci Çavuş, Girbereşik, Batman Merkez, Batman

new.title: Explore Byzantine-era Derzin Castle near Baykan
new.desc: A castle with surviving watchtowers near Adakale (Derzin) village, about 8 km east of Baykan town, dating from the Byzantine period.
new.tip: Reachable by car from Baykan; take water as there are no facilities.

new.title: Pay respects at the Veysel Karani Tomb in Baykan
new.desc: A shrine complex in Baykan district, near the Diyarbakır-Bitlis road, for Veysel Karani, a figure revered in Sufi tradition. The original tomb was demolished in 1967 and rebuilt; commemorative events take place each year on 16-17 May.
new.tip: Modest dress; the best time is the May commemoration, when the site is busiest.

new.title: Ski at Hesarek Ski Centre above Bingöl
new.desc: Opened in 2016 on the slopes of Hesarek Mountain near Dikme village, the centre has a chairlift, a T-bar and pistes for beginners and experienced skiers, within easy reach of Bingöl city.
new.tip: The season is roughly December to March; check snow and lift status locally.
